project_type: Flask web app with YOLO11-seg real-time crack detection
test_framework: No automated tests present - manual verification via running the Flask app
build_command: python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu && pip install -r requirements.txt
test_command: source venv/bin/activate && python -c "from app import app; client=app.test_client(); r=client.get('/health'); assert r.status_code==200, r.data"
verification_instructions: 1. Activate venv. 2. Run python app.py. 3. Verify /health returns 200. 4. Verify /status returns JSON with expected fields. 5. Verify / serves the HTML page.
setup_instructions: dnf install -y mesa-libGL && python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu && pip install -r requirements.txt
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET network mode. No physical cameras available in sandbox. Python 3.9+ available. Must install mesa-libGL for OpenCV.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md found. Standard Python conventions.
key_patterns: inference_core.py: get_model() caches YOLO model, annotate_frame() returns (frame, crack_present). detector.py: Detector class runs background thread, exposes get_latest_jpeg() and get_status(). video_source.py: build_registry() creates named sources with SourceSpec dataclass. app.py: Flask routes serve dashboard, MJPEG stream, JSON status.
directory_structure: Root: app.py (Flask entry), detector.py (inference worker), inference_core.py (YOLO model logic), video_source.py (camera abstraction), best.pt (model weights). templates/dashboard.html (single page). static/style.css, static/js/dashboard.js, static/img/ (SVGs), static/sounds/alert.wav.
